title: Cap. VII: Quarta ratio — Apostle's scope and the safeguard that all have sinned
pass_a_gloss: Next comes the fourth argument. Placeus says the Apostle's purpose will not bear the wording being twisted as Garissoles twists it. At Romans 5:12 Paul started a Christ–Adam comparison precisely so he could affirm entry of sin through one man and of death through sin, with the result that death ranged through the whole human race. The sheer force of one man's single sin in condemning the entire multitude could look astonishing; to keep anyone from thinking ill of God, Paul adds that astonishment is unnecessary because everyone has sinned. Adam entered death for his own sinning; equally, everyone enters death because everyone has sinned.
pass_b_english: The fourth reason follows. The Apostle's scope will not allow them to be turned that way; for the Apostle began at verse 12 (Romans 5:12) to institute a comparison between Christ and Adam in such a manner as to affirm that through one man sin entered, and through sin death, so that death spread abroad upon all men. But because it could seem strange that there was so great force and efficacy in one man's one sin that it should sentence the whole multitude of men to death, lest anyone should suspect anything unworthy of God, he adds that this ought not to seem strange, since all have sinned. As therefore Adam fell into death because he sinned, so also all alike fall into death because all have sinned.
source_text: Sequitur ratio quarta. Scopus Apostoli non patitur ut ita vertantur; coepit enim Apostolus vers. 12. comparationem inter Christum & Adamum instituere eo modo, ut affirmaret per unum hominem peccatum introiisse, & per peccatum mortem, adeo ut mors in omnes homines pervagata sit. Quia vero mirum videri potuit, tantam fuisse in unius hominis uno peccato vim atque efficacitatem, ut totam hominum multitudinem morti addiceret, ne quis indigne quicquam de Deo suspicaretur, addit, id mirum videri non debere, cum omnes peccaverint. Ut igitur Adam in mortem incidit, quia peccavit; sic & omnes pariter in mortem incidunt, quia omnes peccaverunt.
